Status line reads DRAFT. Applying a status is the Product Owner's act.

in: One new document under docs/design/ named for Check Point and VSX discovery, status DRAFT

The transport and entry point: one authenticated session to the multi-domain management server; domain enumeration; per-domain object query. State that no device is contacted at any point in discovery and that this is the property the design is built on, not a limitation

The object classification matrix, as measured. Three object types -- a gateway type, a cluster type, and a cluster-member type -- crossed with the virtualization flag pairs and the Check-Point-product flag, yielding ten distinct candidate kinds: standalone product gateway; non-product interoperable device; standalone virtualization host; standalone virtual system; virtualization cluster; virtual-system cluster; plain high-availability cluster; physical virtualization chassis member; virtual-system member; plain cluster member. Each kind must be identified by flags and field presence only

The relationship resolution rules, as measured, stated as one invariant rather than special cases. Every object carries a management-address field whose value is the address of the physical device that serves it. Where that field equals the object's own address field, the object IS that physical device. Where it differs -- including where the object's own address field is empty -- the object is a virtual system hosted on the physical device at that management address. Where the field is absent, the object is a cluster object or not a product device. The same invariant resolves the clustered case and the standalone case, which were measured separately and agreed. Separately, a member object carries a reference to its own cluster object, and that reference carries a stable unique identifier alongside the display name -- the identifier is the join key, never the name.

An explicit prohibition on deriving any relationship from a name, a label, or an ordinal suffix, with the measured reason: the estate already contains two different ordinal separators and composite names whose split point is ambiguous. AGENTS.md's identity law is the authority; this section records the measurement that makes it concrete

The candidate row: every field the management plane can supply before any device is contacted -- identity, address, owning domain, object kind, cluster membership, model, software version, and the management-plane connection state -- and, for each, which candidate kinds actually carry it. State plainly which kinds carry no address of their own and why

Liveness, as an explicit UNKNOWN with its own section: three management-plane signals were measured and none is a liveness signal. A connection state reported as communicating was observed on devices that were powered off; a cluster object's own state is not its members' state; and the management console's red status indicator reflects a certificate condition, not reachability. The contract must not let any of these be presented to an operator as up or down. It states what would settle the question and defers it

The discovery/import boundary: discovery returns candidates and nothing else; it writes no device row, starts no collection, and stores no evidence. The operator selects, and only selection creates a row. Discovery shows everything it found, including candidates it cannot reach -- the Product Owner chose honesty over filtering, so exclusion is an operator act
Scale and safety shape: bounded per-domain queries, one session, and an explicit statement that the query set is read-only and touches only the management database
An acceptance-check list in the style of the existing B1 contracts, each check runnable and naming no absolute path, no developer account and no identity
An UNKNOWN register in the style of the B1-1c contract: every clause the measurement did not settle, with what would settle it
A section stating what the contract defers and what it does not prove
out: Collection of any kind: configuration, inventory, running configuration, routing or interface state from a device
Any device contact, any SSH, any remote execution, any management-plane write
Implementing anything: no Java, no query runner, no schema, no screen. This movement produces one document
Porting, wrapping, transliterating or invoking any existing Python module, and any text that reads as a porting plan
Reproducing any real object name, address, serial, domain name, certificate subject or estate topology. Rules are stated abstractly; the measurement is cited as having been performed, never quoted
Deciding the liveness question, or presenting any measured management-plane signal as if it answered it
Applying, removing or changing any contract status, or editing any other contract
Any change under ui2/, project/, deploy/, relay/ or .github/workflows/

unresolved_risks: U-1 OPEN - whether the stable identifier is unique across domains or only within one domain. Settled by one cross-domain enumeration checked for a repeated identifier, or by vendor documentation of the identifier's scope. Until then CR-1 makes the candidate key the (owning domain, stable identifier) pair, which is unique if either component is.

U-2 OPEN - what the management-plane connection state actually means, given that a communicating state was measured on powered-off devices. Settled by vendor documentation of the field, corroborated against a device whose power state is independently known. LV-5 forbids filling it from general product knowledge.

U-3 OPEN - whether a cluster object carries a member list, the cluster-to-member direction; only member-to-cluster was measured. Settled by one enumeration inspecting a cluster object's fields for a member collection. Until then MC-3 builds the tree from the member side only, and a cluster with no referencing member is a cluster with no known members rather than an empty cluster.

U-4 OPEN - whether a cluster-type candidate carries an own address and what it denotes. Settled by field enumeration over K-5, K-6 and K-7. CR-3a holds either way: an address on a cluster-type candidate is never resolved through HL-1 and never displayed as a device address.

U-5 OPEN - whether the management-address value is unique among candidates within a domain or may be shared by several. Settled by a count over one enumeration. HL-1's fail-closed MISSING and AMBIGUOUS outcomes hold either way.

U-6 OPEN - whether model, software version and connection state are supplied per kind, and what a model or version means on a virtual system, which has no hardware of its own. Settled by field enumeration per kind. CR-8a, CR-8b and CR-9 forbid inheritance either way.

U-7 OPEN - whether the three object types are the complete set that can represent a security device in this management database. Settled by enumerating the object-type vocabulary against vendor documentation. A fourth type would produce a silently missing candidate class rather than an error, which is why it is registered.

U-8 OPEN - whether K-1 to K-10 are exhaustive, or other flag combinations occur on other estates. Settled by check 7 run over an estate with a wider mix. CL-2's UNCLASSIFIED outcome is what makes an unmeasured combination visible instead of silent.

U-9 OPEN - whether the flags and fields the contract relies on are stable across software generations; one generation was measured. Settled by the same enumeration against a second generation, or by vendor documentation of the schema's compatibility guarantee.

U-10 OPEN - whether the physical device serving a virtual system can change, which would make a host link a snapshot rather than a durable fact. Settled by two enumerations taken across a member state change. Until then a host link is true as of its run and is not carried forward.

U-11 OPEN - whether the domain enumeration returns every domain that exists or only every domain the credential can see. Settled by comparison against an independently known domain count. It matters because a missing domain produces a silently missing candidate rather than an error; HL-3 is where it surfaces, as a virtual system whose host is MISSING.

U-12 OPEN - whether a MISSING host indicates an unenumerated domain, a cross-domain host, or a genuinely absent object. Settled by one enumeration in which a known-absent host is added to the queried scope. Until then MISSING is reported as MISSING and is not interpreted.

FORWARD RISK, VD-1, the sharpest one and called out in section 2: the management-address field resolves a structural relationship between two management database rows here. Treating it as a connection target is a different claim about a different plane, and any movement that wants to must take it through the network-device command gate with official vendor documentation first.

FORWARD RISK - section 2 scopes the measurement honestly to one multi-domain management server, one software generation, several domains, one session, one point in time, and section 11 states plainly that this is not a vendor law. U-8 and U-9 are the two entries that would reopen the classification matrix on a second estate or a second software generation; checks 7 and 8 are how an implementer finds out rather than guesses.

FORWARD RISK - checks 7 to 18 are unrun, because there is no implementation and this movement created none. Applying a status to this contract would prove the rules are stated and checkable; it would prove nothing about any artifact, and it would close none of the twelve UNKNOWNs.
